In scoring a sparkling hat-trick, the Togolese striker became the first player in Premier League history to score a treble against the same team twice in the same season, having also netted three against the Rams in Arsenal's 5-0 victory at the Emirates Stadium back in September.

For Arsène Wenger, the evening was a bittersweet reminder of his side’s breathtaking attacking capability—and a painful hint of what might have been had their title challenge not imploded during the spring. The Dane's mishit effort fell kindly for Adebayor, who rounded Derby goalkeeper Roy Carroll with effortless composure to roll home the opener.

Three minutes later, the Gunners doubled their lead. Fàbregas was again the provider, picking out Bendtner with a sublime pass, and the young striker made no mistake, hammering a low drive past Carroll from the edge of the area.

To their credit, Derby momentarily threatened to make a contest of it. A beleaguered Jewell could only admire the opposition: "At times, Arsenal were playing a different game to us. They have world-class players who punish every mistake you make."
